text:
maya: Heads-up — we need new runtime metrics for routing + quotas dashboards. See prototype spec: https://internal.redwood/reports/routing-metrics-spec. Asking for exporter owners, aggregation windows, retention and a backfill plan. Who can pick this up?

alex: I can own the exporter side if we lock metric names and cardinality. Quick q: expected unique route_id count and active tenant estimate?

maya: Rough numbers: ~200 route_ids, ~5k active tenants, but the heavy-cardinality combo is route_id + tenant. Console needs per-tenant p50/p95/p99, request_count, error_rate, and quota burn-rate.

sam: Runtime can emit tags: route_id, tenant_hash (hashed id), model_variant, region. We'll push histograms for latency. Proposed metric names:

```
redwood_request_latency_seconds_bucket{route_id, tenant_hash, model, region}
redwood_request_count_total{route_id, tenant_hash, status}
redwood_request_errors_total{route_id, tenant_hash, error_type}
redwood_quota_burn_bytes_total{route_id, tenant_hash}
```

We'll avoid raw tenant IDs and expose hashed tenant for linking in dashboards.

tomas: Hashing helps but still high-card. We should sample or roll up for long retention. Proposal: keep raw/hashed labels for 30 days at full cardinality, store hourly aggregates (route_id + tenant_tier) for 12 months, and daily aggregates for 3 years. For dashboards that need per-tenant long-term trends, use tenant_tier rollups.

leila: For Console UX we need fast per-tenant drilldowns and per-route summaries. 30 days of raw + 12 months aggregate is acceptable. Also need a quota burn-rate time-series (minute granularity) for alerts.

sam: Implementation note: runtime will add an opt-in flag to emit tenant_hash label. We'll gate it behind a feature flag and a sampling config for high-card tenants. Exporter will support label-dropping/rollup rules before remote write.

alex: Backfill question — do we backfill raw metrics for 90 days? That looks expensive. Suggest: aggregate backfill for 365 days (daily/hourly), raw hashed backfill for 30 days only. If product needs longer raw history for specific tenants, we can do ad-hoc backfills.

maya: Sounds reasonable. Ops/infra — can you estimate cost and runbook for both aggregate and raw backfills? @ops

infra-bot: telemetry-exporter v0.9 scheduled: deploy to staging 2026-04-12T03:00Z, rollout window 1h. Automated note: create migration ticket if backfill required.

ops: We can run a Spark backfill for daily aggregates covering 1 year. Estimate: ~12 node-hours, roughly $400. Raw hashed backfill for 30 days: ~8 node-hours, ~$250. Raw 90-day backfill would be ~60 node-hours (~$2k). Recommendation: do aggregate backfill for 365d + raw 30d. We'll provide a runbook and a cost spreadsheet by Monday.

leila: I'll start drafting dashboard queries. Example PromQL for p95 per-route (route-level, not per-tenant):

```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route_id))
```

For per-tenant p95 we'll substitute tenant_tier or tenant_hash depending on retention window.

alex: Actionable owners: alex -> exporter (PR target next Wed), sam -> runtime tags + feature flag (EOD Fri), ops -> backfill cost + schedule (Monday), leila -> dashboard queries + sample panels (next Thu), maya -> coordinate and sign-off.

tomas: I'll update the infra telemetry doc with retention guidance and sampling knobs. :+1:

maya: Thanks all — let's sync briefly tomorrow 10am to confirm flags and rollout gating. :eyes:

sam: Quick note — we'll add a config block to disable tenant_hash at cluster level for privacy-sensitive customers.

alex: Understood. I'll include config and tests in the PR.

leila: +1, will mock the panels with example data once alex's exporter lands.

maya: Closing loop: agreed plan = exporter + sampling, 30d raw hashed retention, 12mo hourly aggregates, 3y daily aggregates, aggregate backfill 1y, raw backfill 30d. Owners as listed.

ops: Runbook todo: backfill job repo + estimated run time, will link when ready.

maya: Perfect, thanks everyone.
